_note: SERP snapshot for the information-gain gate. The research pass for this topic searched English-language coverage of GACC Announcement No. 136 of 2026 (container suitability inspection for exported perishable and frozen food). English coverage is thin and sits in three places: a freight forwarder's client advisory, a seafood trade newswire brief, and a Hong Kong trade-promotion research note. All three describe the filing channel and the 21-day validity. None prices the window: there is no per-container cost arithmetic anywhere in the English coverage, which is what this article adds. Chinese-language coverage is more detailed and does carry the Article 51 fine maxima, but it prices no lapse either. customs.gov.cn, tid.gov.hk, mofcom.gov.cn and chinatax.gov.cn are official publishers and are excluded from the competitor denominator automatically.
_keyword: China container suitability inspection perishable frozen food exports 2026

results.title: Policy Radar: 21 Days Only: China Reefer Container Rule Starts Oct 1
results.snippet: GACC Announcement No. 136 forces a fitness filing before stuffing. The result expires in 21 days, on its own. Customs validates the fitness result at export declaration, and a failed validation means the declaration is rejected outright.

results.title: IN BRIEF - China Digitalizes Container Controls for Perishable and Frozen Food
results.snippet: From October 1, 2026, China Customs will require pre-loading container checks via the International Trade Single Window. Electronic validation will be mandatory for export clearance, with approved results valid for 21 days.

results.title: GAC Optimises Perishable and Frozen Food Export Inspection Measures
results.snippet: China's customs administration has optimised the inspection model for containers shipping perishable and frozen food for export, moving from enterprise pre-inspection with customs sampling to a compliance declaration with customs review and risk-based checks.
